error.signature: AI tells a traveler that drugs are 'legal' in Portugal, or that carrying any amount for personal use carries no legal consequence

verdict.summary: Lei n.o 30/2000 reclassified the acquisition, possession, and consumption of drugs for personal use as a 'contraordenacao' (administrative offense) rather than a crime, when the quantity held does not exceed the amount needed for an average 10-day individual supply. It never legalized drugs: buying, selling, trafficking, and cultivation, as well as possession beyond that 10-day reference quantity, remain criminal offenses. Cases within the threshold go to a regional Comissao para a Dissuasao da Toxicodependencia (CDT), which can still impose fines or other sanctions - it is unlawful, just not prosecuted in criminal court.

dead_ends.action: Tell a traveler or resident that drugs are 'legal' in Portugal, or that carrying drugs carries no legal consequence
dead_ends.why_fails: Lei 30/2000 (Article 2) makes acquisition, possession, and consumption for personal use within a 10-day reference quantity a 'contraordenacao' - an administrative offense handled by a regional Dissuasion Commission (CDT), not a decriminalized-into-nonexistence act. It is still unlawful and can lead to fines or other sanctions; trafficking, dealing, and cultivation beyond personal-use quantities remain criminal offenses under separate narcotics legislation.
dead_ends.condition: Personal possession/consumption of a substance covered by Lei 30/2000
dead_ends.common_misconception: That 'decriminalized' means 'legal' - Portugal moved enforcement from criminal court to an administrative panel; it never made drug possession lawful.

dead_ends.action: Assume any quantity carried 'for personal use' is treated the same and stays out of the criminal system
dead_ends.why_fails: The law only shields possession up to the amount needed for an average 10-day individual supply. Exceeding that quantity is treated as an indication of trafficking intent, referred to a judicial authority, and only excluded from prosecution if the person proves it was exclusively for personal consumption.
dead_ends.condition: Possession exceeding the 10-day personal-use reference quantity

workarounds.action: Explain that possession/use within the 10-day personal-use threshold is an administrative offense handled by a regional Dissuasion Commission (CDT) - not a criminal court - but can still mean fines or mandatory measures; it is not risk-free or 'legal'
workarounds.condition: General explanation of Portugal's drug policy

workarounds.action: Warn that buying, selling, or possessing quantities beyond the personal-use threshold remains a criminal offense, and that Portugal's framework (documented by the Library of Congress comparative report) is decriminalization, not legalization
workarounds.condition: Trafficking, dealing, or quantities beyond personal-use thresholds
